About tipright.app

Tipping in the US is expected for most personal services, but knowing the right amount isn't always obvious. tipright.app gives you a specific number in seconds, no ranges, no "it depends," just the amount for your service.

Every calculator shows five tip levels at once, 10% through 25%, and highlights the standard for that specific service. You can split the tip with friends or just compare the options. Everything calculates as you type. No button, no reload.

The shareable URL feature means you can calculate your tip and send the link to whoever you're with. They'll see the same numbers with no setup required.

Frequently asked questions about tipping in the US

How much should you tip in the US?
The standard tip across most US services is 15–20% of the pre-tax total. For restaurants, salons, tattoos, and massage, 20% is the common benchmark. For flat-rate services like hotel housekeeping and valet, tip $2–5 per interaction.
Is tipping mandatory in the United States?
Not legally, but it’s strongly expected for most personal services. Many tipped workers earn as little as $2.13/hour federally. Tips are core income, not a bonus. Not tipping for satisfactory service at a restaurant or salon is considered rude.
What is the standard tip percentage?
20% is the widely accepted standard for most personal services in the US. 15% is the floor for acceptable service. 25%+ is right for exceptional work or specialized services like custom tattoos or complex color treatments.
Should you tip on the pre-tax or post-tax amount?
Tip on the pre-tax subtotal. Tax goes to the government, not the service provider. On a $90 bill with $10 tax, tip on $90, that’s $18, not $20. Pre-tax tipping is the standard convention.
How do you split a tip with friends?
Calculate the full tip on the total bill, then divide by the number of people. A $200 bill with a 20% tip is $40 total, or $10 per person for 4 people. Every calculator on tipright.app has a built-in split feature.
Do you have to tip for every service?
Most face-to-face personal services expect a tip: restaurants, salons, tattoo studios, massage, barbers, and similar. Tipping is optional at fast casual counters and not expected for medical professionals or retail staff.
